title: Wall library
description: A library of wall build-ups for the IngeTrazo openings extension. Edit it in any editor that understands JSON Schema and it will tell you about a misspelled role or a thickness that is not a thickness while you type, instead of when you import it. Import the file back through Extensions ▸ Doors & windows ▸ Import wall types…; the import checks every wall and reports what it could not read.

$schema.description: Where this file's schema is. Keep walls.schema.json beside the library and your editor validates as you type.

locale.description: Which library this is, and the prefix every key must carry: nl, en-GB, de, es-ES, es-PE. An entry without one belongs to the library named here.

country.description: Free text, for a person reading the file.

note.description: What this library is and what a draft means. Copied into every export.

walls.description: The build-ups. Ten external and ten internal is what the shipped libraries aim for.

key.description: Stable identity, starting with the library code and a dot: nl.spouwmuur.100-120-100. A document may cite it, so renaming a key detaches a wall from its type — change the thicknesses instead.

legacy.description: The name this wall was known by before the library existed (spouwmuur, binnenwand). Documents cite it; do not invent new ones.

locale.description: Only needed when a file holds walls for more than one country. An imported wall always gets one.

enumDescriptions: A wall to the outside: weather, insulation, the facade.
A wall between two inside spaces, or between dwellings.

name.description: The name, per language. At least one language, and en-GB is the one everything falls back to.

source.description: Where the build-up came from: a standard, a detail, a practice. Say enough that somebody can check it.

checked.description: The date this entry was last looked at.

reviewed.description: true only when a PERSON has checked this build-up against what is actually built. It must be true or false — the string "false" is not false, and the import refuses it.

note.description: What this build-up cannot say about itself: studs counted as insulation, a membrane thinner than a layer, a requirement it does not meet.

performance.description: Present and deliberately empty. This extension does not compute or claim an Rc or U-value; the fields are here to be filled in from a source, or to be written into IFC later.

rc.description: m²K/W, if a source gives one. Not computed.

u.description: W/m²K. Maps onto Pset_WallCommon.ThermalTransmittance when the export carries it.

skins.description: The layers, from the outside in. The wall is centred on the line drawn in plan, so this list reads left to right as you walk the path.

enumDescriptions: The masonry that faces the weather.
An air space, ventilated or not.
Mineral wool, EPS, PIR — whatever fills the depth.
Stuc, putz, revoco, tarrajeo: the cement skin outside.
The plaster inside a masonry wall.
A board: plasterboard, boarding, dry lining.
A membrane. Thinner than a skin may be (3 mm), so it is a note rather than a layer.
A void for pipes and cables.
A rainscreen: timber, brick slips, panels.
An outer masonry leaf of a veneer wall.
Concrete, brick or block carrying the load.

thickness.description: MILLIMETRES, not metres. 100 is 100 mm. A layer thinner than 3 mm is a membrane and cannot be a skin.

note.description: Why this layer is the number it is, if that needs saying.
